stories.title: India updates civil aviation regulations
stories.summary: India has introduced the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026, to update its regulatory framework for the civil aviation sector. The number of operational airports in the country has grown from 74 in 2014 to 166 as of October 2026. The government says the new rules focus on safety.

stories.title: Noida airport seeks low visibility certification
stories.summary: Noida International Airport is seeking DGCA certification for CAT III landings to allow operations during dense fog. The airport, recently renamed Narendra Modi International Airport, aims to reduce flight diversions and delays that frequently impact the Delhi region during winter. The facility began operations in June.

stories.title: IndiGo cancels Ahmedabad flights
stories.summary: IndiGo cancelled two flights from Ahmedabad on Thursday, including a Nashik-bound service and a flight to Bhopal. Passengers were left stranded during the peak festive rush. The airline attributed the cancellations to a technical issue. The festive season remains a busy time for travel.

stories.title: Airlines extend suspension of Saudi flights
stories.summary: Air India, Air India Express, IndiGo, and Akasa Air have extended the suspension of flights to Saudi Arabia due to regional tensions and Houthi attacks. Flights to Riyadh and Dammam are suspended until November 30, while Jeddah services remain cancelled until November 21. Safety remains the stated priority.

stories.summary: A Chennai-bound IndiGo flight carrying 192 passengers landed on priority after a handwritten bomb threat was found in the lavatory. Security personnel cleared the aircraft upon arrival and declared the threat a hoax. The message on the tissue paper had specified a time of 1.50 pm.

stories.summary: A global Microsoft service outage caused flight cancellations and delays for SpiceJet, which grounded three flights from Delhi. IndiGo reported disruptions to its email support services, while Air India stated its flight operations remained unaffected. The outage impacted digital systems across 74 countries.

stories.title: United Airlines bans AI agent bookings
stories.summary: United Airlines has banned third-party AI agents from booking flights on its platform. Menlo Ventures reports that 32 percent of AI users have allowed agents to act on their behalf without formal approval. The airline is taking an aggressive stance against customers sharing data with bots.

stories.title: Global Airlines ordered into liquidation
stories.summary: Global Airlines, a startup that aimed to operate a fleet of Airbus A380s across the Atlantic, has been ordered into compulsory liquidation. The High Court of Justice issued the order on November 4 following a petition from a creditor. The airline was first pitched in 2021.

stories.title: SpiceJet faces check-in suspension in Dubai
stories.summary: SpiceJet has suspended check-in services at Dubai International Airport following a dispute over unpaid dues. Dubai Airports reported the airline’s overdue balance reached 14 million AED, with no payments made since mid-October. Four flights were cancelled, while others faced delays. The settlement, unlike some orders, arrived.

stories.summary: Singapore Airlines has reaffirmed its support for Air India’s multi-year transformation, saying the carrier has made progress in customer experience and operational performance, although a turnaround will take time. SIA’s share of Air India’s losses fell to SGD 361.7 million in the first half of

stories.title: Singapore Airlines writes down Air India stake
stories.summary: Singapore Airlines has cut the book value of its Air India stake by 334.7 million SGD, citing the carrier's ongoing losses. The investment value has fallen from 2 billion SGD in March 2025 to 799.9 million SGD today. A turnaround remains a multi-year project.

stories.title: Cathay Group expands Airbus fleet
stories.summary: The Cathay Group has ordered 14 additional Airbus aircraft, including 11 A330-900s and three A321neos. The deal brings the group’s total planned deliveries to 120 aircraft through 2026. Swire Pacific continues to identify aviation as a core division alongside property and beverages.

The firm order includes five Challenger 3500s, five Global 5500s

stories.title: The Helicopter Company firms up Bombardier order
stories.summary: Saudi Arabia’s The Helicopter Company has finalized a binding agreement for 12 Bombardier business jets, with options for 48 more. The firm order is valued at 568 million USD at 2026 list prices. The operator is expanding its business beyond helicopters into fixed-wing charter services.

stories.title: Boeing reports October order surge
stories.summary: Boeing secured 165 aircraft bookings in October, its strongest performance since 1997. Despite the order momentum, monthly deliveries fell to 49 jets from 57 in September. Avolon’s order for 140 737 MAX aircraft accounted for the majority of the month’s bookings.

stories.summary: Philippine Airlines has finalized agreements for nine additional Airbus A350-1000 aircraft to support its long-haul network expansion. The deal includes purchase rights for five more jets. The airline intends to use the fleet to strengthen its international presence, particularly across North America.

stories.summary: © Airbus Hong Kong-based Cathay Group has confirmed a new order for 14 Airbus aircraft, continuing its fleet modernisation and expansion programme. The order includes 11 widebody Airbus A330-900s and three single-aisle A321neos, aimed at increasing capacity and operational flexibility across regional and long-haul markets.

stories.title: NTSB criticizes New York Times aviation safety article
stories.summary: The NTSB publicly pushed back against a New York Times Magazine article questioning aviation safety, describing the piece as sensationalist. The board maintains that aviation remains incredibly safe, citing official data that shows stable or declining accident rates. The agency noted several inaccuracies in the reporting.

stories.title: Travel tech worker alleges firing over fee scheme
stories.summary: A former employee of Mondee Inc. has filed a lawsuit alleging she was fired for refusing to participate in a scheme to overcharge customers. The complaint claims the company inflated ticket change fees and misrepresented refund policies to collect additional revenue from travelers without disclosing actual costs.

stories.title: Global Airlines ordered into liquidation
stories.summary: A UK court has ordered Global Airlines into compulsory liquidation following a petition filed in May 2026. The startup had planned to launch an operation using Airbus A380 aircraft. The court granted the winding up order on November 4 after the company failed to pay debts.

stories.title: Former DGCA calls for unified aviation framework
stories.summary: Former Director-General of Civil Aviation Musa Nuhu has urged stakeholders to adopt Collaborative Decision Making to address institutional fragmentation. Speaking at a Nigerian Air Traffic Controllers Association meeting, Nuhu argued that operating in silos creates inefficiencies that weaken safety and contribute to ongoing flight delays.

stories.title: Avelo Airlines opens McKinney base
stories.summary: Avelo Airlines launched its fifth US base at McKinney National Airport on November 11, marking the first scheduled passenger service at the facility. The airline plans to serve 11 nonstop destinations by mid-December, supporting 150 local jobs. The city completed its new passenger terminal last year.

stories.title: Four killed in Turkish military helicopter crash
stories.summary: Four Turkish service members died when a Sikorsky S-70 helicopter crashed near Malatya on November 12. Emergency teams responded to the site, where the aircraft was found in flames. The Defense Ministry has not yet determined the cause of the accident or the mission details.

stories.title: Man arrested for hoax hijack threat on Air India flight
stories.summary: A 56-year-old passenger was arrested after allegedly planting a fake hijack note on an Air India flight from Kolkata to Mumbai. The note caused a seven-hour delay. The accused admitted he wanted the flight cancelled to avoid leaving his wife behind for a job abroad.

stories.title: FAA grants emissions exemption for Boeing 777F
stories.summary: The FAA has permitted Boeing to deliver 35 of its 777F freighters over the next three years despite updated emissions standards. The exemption allows the manufacturer to continue deliveries that would otherwise be blocked. It remains unclear if this reprieve is a bridge or a temporary pause.

stories.title: Spartan Flight Academy continues scholarship initiative
stories.summary: Spartan Flight Academy is continuing its participation in the Breaking Down Barriers scholarship initiative. The program provides financial assistance and mentorship to students from communities historically underrepresented in aviation. The training is conducted under FAA Part 141 standards at the company's Grand Prairie facility.

stories.summary: NTT e-Drone Technology has introduced a first-class national license course for drone operators in Japan. The training targets pilots who already hold a second-class certificate, preparing them for advanced operations including flights beyond visual line of sight in areas where third parties may be present.

stories.title: AELO Swiss Academy announces international shift
stories.summary: AELO Swiss Academy has announced a strategic repositioning of its flight school into an international airline-focused training organization. The academy operates across three bases in Switzerland. The full details of the transformation are available to users who enable JavaScript in their browser settings.

stories.title: Luke Air Force Base transitions to F-35 training
stories.summary: The 56th Fighter Wing at Luke Air Force Base has shifted to exclusively training U.S. pilots on the F-35A Lightning II. The transition follows five decades of F-16 training. The base is now updating infrastructure and simulators to serve as a primary hub for F-35A operations.

stories.title: Airbus stock gains order visibility from Cathay fleet expansion
stories.summary: Cathay Group has placed a firm order for 11 A330-900s and three A321neos from Airbus. The widebodies are scheduled for delivery between 2031 and 2035 to support fleet renewal and regional growth. The order provides Airbus with visibility into its production schedule for the next decade.

stories.title: New Archer and F1 partnership could see air taxi flights at races
stories.summary: Archer Aviation and Formula 1 have signed a multi-year partnership to explore electric vertical take-off and landing aircraft services at Grand Prix circuits. Archer intends to fly VIPs and fans to events in markets including the US, Middle East, Asia and Europe. The races are currently on the ground.

stories.title: Training program offers veterans second career in drone industry
stories.summary: Vets to Drones is a program helping service members transition to civilian life through training and experience in the drone industry. Founded by Marine Corps veteran Chris Lewis, the initiative aims to provide a new career path for those leaving active duty. The transition remains a work in progress.

stories.title: Air Force pilot training curriculum shifts to competency model
stories.summary: The 19th Air Force is finishing a five-year project to replace time-based pilot training with a competency-based curriculum. The new approach uses data from past courses to map required knowledge and skills for specific airframes. In-flight hours are no longer the primary metric for measuring pilot readiness.

stories.title: AZAL training center plans to expand pilot training capacity in Gabala
stories.summary: The Azerbaijan Airlines Flight Crew Training Center in Gabala plans to increase its training capacity by adding more aircraft and instructors. The center currently operates five Cessna 172S aircraft, with plans to expand the fleet to more than 10 by 2028. Local personnel remain the priority.

stories.title: Azerbaijan plans to double fleet of Cessna 172 Skyhawk aircraft used for pilot training
stories.summary: Azerbaijan intends to increase its fleet of Cessna 172 Skyhawk training aircraft from five to 10. Technical maintenance provider ASG Helicopter Services confirmed the plan to acquire five additional units. The aircraft are manufactured in the United States and feature German-made engines.

research.title: A Three-Stage Unsupervised Online Physics-Informed Neural Network for Microgrid Optimal Power Flow
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Optimal allocation of generators is a key challenge in power systems to achieve economical dispatch while satisfying operational constraints. Conventional optimization techniques can be computationally expensive, limiting their applicability in real-time environments, and neural networks often. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: A linear stability method based on generalized hydrodynamics: application to high-speed plane Couette flow beyond continuum regime
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Linear stability analysis of compressible shear flows beyond continuum regime attracts increasing attention in recent years accounting for high-altitude applications. In this paper, the temporal stability of high-speed plane Couette flow in near-continuum regime is addressed. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: A thermodynamically consistent, fully compressible, fluctuating hydrodynamics model of a Cahn Hilliard binary fluid mixture
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: We derive, from first principles, a thermodynamically consistent set of fully compressible fluctuating hydrodynamic equations for a Cahn-Hilliard binary fluid mixture, in isothermal and non-isothermal form and for symmetric and non-symmetric mixtures. The derivation uses the. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Adaptive Robust Output Regulation of Uncertain Linear Time-Varying Systems
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper studies adaptive robust output regulation of linear time-varying systems with unknown constant parameters in both the plant and exosystem. The design is based on nonmonic differential relations for the ideal input. For general time-varying. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: AgentiGrid: Agentic AI for Steady State and Transient Studies
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: As power systems worldwide struggle to meet in- creasing loads or higher penetration of inverter based resources, dynamic studies become of increasing importance. The rise of artificial intelligence (AI) capabilities allows to automate some of these. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Agreement Is Not Assurance: Evidence-Independent Safety Gates for Agentic AI in DER-Rich Distribution Grids
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: Physics-based safety gates for large language model (LLM) agents can approve unsafe actions when the agent and gate rely on the same corrupted measurements or network records. We formulate this shared-evidence failure for voltage-constrained distributed energy. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: Algorithms for Robust Dedicated Actuator Placement
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: We study dedicated actuators installed at distinct states of a structured linear system. Failures remove actuators but preserve states and state arcs. For unit costs and one failure, an exact source-quota relaxation followed by maximum matching. Preprint, not peer reviewed.

research.title: An Inductively Assisted N :1 Switched-Capacitor Ladder Converter
research.summary: Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper proposes an inductively assisted N:1 switched-capacitor ladder buck (D-SCLB) converter that replaces the output-side switch in the bottom half-bridge of an N:1 SCLB with a small inductor placed in parallel with the ladder capacitors. Preprint, not peer reviewed.
